themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Three water quality complaints filed THIS WEEK (vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks) represent a 1100% spike with z-score 6.35, signaling a potential contamination or distribution system failure affecting Morningside Heights residents.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints filed this week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
High statistical significance suggests systemic issue rather than isolated complaints
Concurrent food poisoning spike (3 complaints this week vs. 0.2 avg) may indicate water-related contamination
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to determine if water main break, boil water advisory, or contamination event has occurred in CD109
Interview affected residents about water discoloration, odor, or taste changes; verify if complaints concentrated in specific buildings or blocks

themes_detail.label: Homeless Assistance Requests Surge
themes_detail.summary: Thirteen homeless person assistance complaints filed THIS WEEK versus 1.8 weekly average (643% spike, z-score 5.67) indicate a sudden concentration of unhoused individuals or a crisis triggering 311 calls in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 13 homeless person assistance complaints this week vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (643% spike, z-score: 5.67)
Aligns with recurring community board budget request for 'outreach services to homebound older adults' — suggests chronic underfunding of social services
Non-emergency police matter complaints also spiked 229% last week (7 vs. 2.1 avg), potentially connected to street-level disorder
reporting_angles: Identify if complaints are geographically clustered (e.g., near subway stations, parks, or shelter locations) and whether a specific encampment or influx has emerged
Interview residents and local business owners; contact NYC Department of Homeless Services to assess shelter capacity and outreach deployment in the district

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Spike This Week
themes_detail.summary: Three food poisoning complaints filed last week (vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks) represent a 1100% spike with z-score 6.35, paired with six food establishment violation complaints 2 weeks ago (336% spike), suggesting compromised food safety infrastructure in the neighborhood.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
6 food establishment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average (336% spike, z-score: 4.66)
Combined pattern suggests systematic food safety failures; possible connection to water quality spike if contamination affected food prep
reporting_angles: FOIL NYC Health Department inspection records for Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights restaurants and food vendors filed in past 2 weeks; identify pattern of violations
Interview residents who filed complaints; survey local restaurants about recent water, supplier, or operational issues; investigate if single venue or outbreak or multiple independent incidents

themes_detail.label: Vendor and Illegal Posting Enforcement Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Six vendor enforcement complaints filed THIS WEEK (500% spike, z-score 5.0) and five illegal posting complaints 3 weeks ago (1233% spike, z-score 4.66) indicate breakdown in street-level code enforcement and possible commercial disorder in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 6 vendor enforcement complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
5 illegal posting complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (1233% spike, z-score: 4.66)
Suggests either influx of unregulated street vending or failure of Department of Consumer Affairs enforcement capacity
reporting_angles: Identify if illegal vendors are concentrated in commercial corridors (Amsterdam Ave, Broadway, 125th St) or near Columbia University campus
Interview Department of Consumer Affairs about staffing, enforcement priorities, and response times; document specific vendor types and illegal postings (ads, political signage, graffiti)

themes_detail.label: Building Exterior Damage Spike 3 Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Six 'outside building' complaints filed 3 weeks ago versus 0.8 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 6.33) suggest widespread facade, cornice, or structural deterioration, though complaint volume has not remained elevated this week.
evidence: 6 outside building complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 6.33)
330 active alteration permits filed in past 90 days; may indicate large renovation wave straining inspection or quality oversight
Paint/plaster complaints ranked 7th in 90-day volume (591 complaints), suggesting chronic building maintenance issues
reporting_angles: Determine if spike corresponded to recent weather event (heavy wind, rain) or if related to ongoing renovation work and lack of safety protocols
FOIL DOB violation records for 'outside building' hazards filed 3 weeks ago to identify specific buildings and assess if pattern has continued
